pages.quiz:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #1
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A family keeps a Tulsi plant at home. What is a good daily habit for them? (1 mark)
   A. Water it every morning
   B. Cut it down
   C. Burn it
   D. Ignore it

2. What does water often stand for in religious life? (1 mark)
   A. Anger
   B. Noise
   C. Purity and a clean heart
   D. Hunger

3. Which sacred river of India did the lesson say is honoured as a goddess in the stories? (1 mark)
   A. Beas
   B. Rijubalika
   C. Nzoia
   D. Ganga

4. Where does the River Ganga begin? (1 mark)
   A. In Lake Victoria
   B. In the Rift Valley
   C. In the Himalaya mountains
   D. At the Indian Ocean coast

5. In the seed activity, what happens to the seeds that get no water? (1 mark)
   A. They turn blue
   B. They turn into stones
   C. They do not grow
   D. They grow tall fast

6. What does Ahimsa mean? (1 mark)
   A. Paying taxes
   B. Telling stories
   C. Not hurting any living being
   D. Eating late

7. Which city did Guru Ram Das Ji start? (1 mark)
   A. Nairobi
   B. Mombasa
   C. Varanasi
   D. Amritsar

8. A snake is often shown with statues of which Tirthankar? (1 mark)
   A. Guru Ram Das
   B. Parshvanath
   C. Buddha
   D. Narsimha

9. What are the Laavan? (1 mark)
   A. Hymns sung at a Sikh wedding
   B. Prayers before meals
   C. Festival songs of Maha Shivratri
   D. Yoga postures

10. Who brought Siddhartha up after his mother died? (1 mark)
   A. His aunt Mahaprajapati Gotami
   B. A king
   C. A teacher
   D. His cousin Devadatta

11. Who declared that Sikhs should follow the Granth as their Guru? (1 mark)
   A. Guru Gobind Singh Ji
   B. Sigala
   C. Ram
   D. Guru Amar Das Ji

12. Which Jain scripture gives advice on a disciplined life? (1 mark)
   A. Dhammapada
   B. Ramayan
   C. Sigalovada Sutta
   D. Uttaradhyayan Sutra

13. Which is a bad habit during prayer? (1 mark)
   A. Folding hands
   B. Laughing or talking
   C. Sitting still
   D. Listening

14. What is a good posture for prayer? (1 mark)
   A. Jump around
   B. Eat snacks
   C. Lie down and talk
   D. Sit calmly with hands folded

15. What does sakha mean in the prayer? (1 mark)
   A. God
   B. Mother
   C. Wealth
   D. Friend

16. Which words begin the well-known Saraswati Vandana? (1 mark)
   A. Om Namah Shivaya
   B. Ya Kundendu Tushara Hara Dhavala
   C. Om Bhur Bhuvah Svah
   D. Twameva mata cha pita twameva

17. What is the lesson of the Harishchandra story? (1 mark)
   A. Truth is worth more than wealth or comfort
   B. Lies are useful
   C. Promises are not important
   D. Wealth is everything

18. Why is integrity compared to a strong wall? (1 mark)
   A. Because it is heavy
   B. Because it is tall
   C. One weak brick can make it fall
   D. Because walls are white

19. Which is polite when alighting? (1 mark)
   A. Run into the road
   B. Thank the driver or conductor
   C. Leave rubbish
   D. Push others

20. What should you do if your knees hurt in Vajra Asana? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore it
   B. Stop and come out of the pose
   C. Stay for an hour
   D. Push harder

21. What should you practise yoga on? (1 mark)
   A. A mat
   B. A wet floor
   C. A road
   D. A tree

22. Which three things does yoga join? (1 mark)
   A. Rivers, trees and fire
   B. Body, breath and mind
   C. Books, pens and paper
   D. Water, soil and air

23. What is the benefit of Sasankasana? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the arms shorter
   B. It stretches the back and shoulders and relaxes
   C. It is useless
   D. It cures every disease

24. What is the correct way to sit for Pranayam? (1 mark)
   A. Lying on the stomach
   B. Slouching
   C. With a straight back and relaxed body
   D. Standing on one leg

25. How do we breathe in yoga? (1 mark)
   A. Through the nose, slowly
   B. Not at all
   C. In gasps
   D. Only through the mouth quickly

26. In Kapaal Bhaati, which part of the breath is quick? (1 mark)
   A. The breath in
   B. Both are held
   C. Neither
   D. The breath out

27. What does Artha mean? (1 mark)
   A. War
   B. A river
   C. Prayer
   D. Honest wealth and the things we need

28. Which principle is about kindness to all living beings? (1 mark)
   A. Punarjanam
   B. Prani Daya
   C. Paramatma
   D. Purushartha

29. What does Moksha mean? (1 mark)
   A. A meal
   B. Freedom of the soul
   C. A song
   D. A game

30. What is patriotism? (1 mark)
   A. Love for one's country
   B. Love for sweets
   C. Dislike of others
   D. Fear of others

31. In which year did Kenya gain internal self-government? (1 mark)
   A. 1963
   B. 1980
   C. 1950
   D. 2010

32. What is the abhishek? (1 mark)
   A. Ringing a bell
   B. Bathing the Shiva Linga with water and milk
   C. Lighting a bonfire
   D. Reading a book

33. What is a jagaran or vigil? (1 mark)
   A. A meal
   B. Eating a big meal
   C. Staying awake at night to pray and sing
   D. A race

34. In which months does Paryushan usually occur? (1 mark)
   A. August or September
   B. June
   C. December
   D. February or March

35. What is a rite or ritual? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of food
   B. A river
   C. A school subject
   D. A special action done in a set way at a festival

36. Which day is linked with Mars? (1 mark)
   A. Friday
   B. Tuesday
   C. Saturday
   D. Thursday

37. Mangal is the Indian name for which planet? (1 mark)
   A. Jupiter
   B. Mars
   C. Venus
   D. Mercury

38. Which activity helps you learn the days and planets? (1 mark)
   A. Copying from a book
   B. Making a decorated calendar
   C. Painting
   D. Hiding the calendar

39. Which planet is closest to the Sun? (1 mark)
   A. Saturn
   B. Mars
   C. Mercury
   D. Venus

40. Ravi is another name for which heavenly body? (1 mark)
   A. Venus
   B. Mars
   C. The Sun
   D. The Moon

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Why should a passenger wait for the vehicle to stop before getting off? (2 marks)

42. Give three uses of the Indian traditional calendar. (3 marks)

43. Explain how a maize farm uses all five elements. (4 marks)

44. Explain how learners can include friends with special needs in yoga. (5 marks)

45. Describe the day of prayers for a child. (5 marks)

46. Write three main teachings of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji. (3 marks)

47. Name the months of the Indian traditional calendar in which Maha Shivratri and Paryushan fall. (3 marks)

48. Explain what Punarjanam means. (3 marks)

49. Match the days to the planets: Budhvaar, Guruvaar, Shukravaar. (3 marks)

50. Discuss how people of different faiths show respect for water and trees. (5 marks)

51. Give two benefits of daily prayer. (2 marks)

52. Explain how the days of the week are related to the solar system. (3 marks)

53. Describe how a child can follow all five principles in one day. (5 marks)

54. Tell the story of Prahlad and Hiranyakashipu in three sentences. (3 marks)

55. Name the two Ramayan kaands studied in this lesson. (2 marks)

56. List the five principles of Dharma studied in the lesson. (2 marks)

57. Match four scriptures with their faiths. (4 marks)

58. Explain the importance of celebrating Madaraka Day. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #1 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Water it every morning
   Watering the Tulsi is part of caring for it.

2. C — Purity and a clean heart
   Because water cleans, it is a sign of purity.

3. D — Ganga
   In the stories Ganga is honoured as a goddess.

4. C — In the Himalaya mountains
   The Ganga starts high in the Himalaya and flows across northern India.

5. C — They do not grow
   Seeds need water to sprout.

6. C — Not hurting any living being
   Ahimsa is non-violence in thought, word and action.

7. D — Amritsar
   The city that grew into Amritsar.

8. B — Parshvanath
   The snake is a sign of Parshvanath.

9. A — Hymns sung at a Sikh wedding
   Guru Ram Das Ji wrote these wedding hymns.

10. A — His aunt Mahaprajapati Gotami
   His mother's sister looked after him.

11. A — Guru Gobind Singh Ji
   He was the tenth Guru.

12. D — Uttaradhyayan Sutra
   It teaches Ahimsa, truth and control of anger.

13. B — Laughing or talking
   We should be quiet and respectful.

14. D — Sit calmly with hands folded
   Calm sitting is respectful.

15. D — Friend
   Sakha means friend.

16. B — Ya Kundendu Tushara Hara Dhavala
   This is the opening line.

17. A — Truth is worth more than wealth or comfort
   The king chose truth.

18. C — One weak brick can make it fall
   Small lies can weaken trust.

19. B — Thank the driver or conductor
   Thanking shows good manners.

20. B — Stop and come out of the pose
   Do not force the body.

21. A — A mat
   A clean mat is best.

22. B — Body, breath and mind
   Yoga joins these three.

23. B — It stretches the back and shoulders and relaxes
   It gently stretches and relaxes.

24. C — With a straight back and relaxed body
   A straight back helps breathing.

25. A — Through the nose, slowly
   We breathe calmly through the nose.

26. D — The breath out
   The breath is pushed out in short pulls.

27. D — Honest wealth and the things we need
   Artha is earning in an honest way.

28. B — Prani Daya
   Prani Daya is compassion.

29. B — Freedom of the soul
   Moksha is the highest goal.

30. A — Love for one's country
   Patriotism is love for our country.

31. A — 1963
   On 1 June 1963.

32. B — Bathing the Shiva Linga with water and milk
   Abhishek is ritual bathing of the murti or symbol.

33. C — Staying awake at night to pray and sing
   Devotees stay awake.

34. A — August or September
   It falls in Bhadrapada.

35. D — A special action done in a set way at a festival
   Examples are lighting a lamp or raising a flag.

36. B — Tuesday
   Mangalvaar.

37. B — Mars
   Mangal is Mars, the red planet.

38. B — Making a decorated calendar
   Decorating helps memory.

39. C — Mercury
   Mercury is nearest to the Sun.

40. C — The Sun
   Ravi is the Sun.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Moving while the vehicle is moving can cause falls and accidents.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for danger, 1 mark for safety.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fixing festival dates, choosing days for prayers and family events, keeping tradition alive (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: The soil is Prithvi, rain and river water are Jal, the sun's heat is Agni, the wind that carries pollen is Vayu, and the open sky is Akash.
   Working / marking points: Award 1 mark for each element linked correctly to the farm, up to 4.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: They can do breathing slowly, take seated poses, help hold the chart or take photos, and be encouraged by their partners. Everyone's effort is respected.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points and 1 mark for respect.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: In the morning, the Gayatri Mantra and the Saraswati Vandana before study; at midday before meals, Twameva Mata cha Pita Twameva; in the evening, thanks to God. Also sit calmly and fold hands.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part of the day, 1 mark for manners.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: There is one God, all human beings are equal, earn honestly and share with others, and serve without expecting a reward (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each teaching.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Maha Shivratri in Phalguna and Paryushan in Bhadrapada.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each and 1 mark for correct spelling.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Punarjanam is rebirth. The soul does not die but takes a new body until it reaches Moksha.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rebirth, 1 mark for the soul, 1 mark for Moksha.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Mercury, Jupiter, Venus.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

50. (5 marks)
   Answer: Hindus honour the Ganga and Tulsi; Sikhs remember the Beas and the Ber tree; Jains honour the Rijubalika and the Sal tree; Buddhists honour the Bodhi tree. All value water and trees and take care of them.
   Working / marking points: Award 1 mark for each faith correctly described, up to 4 marks, and 1 mark for the idea that all faiths show respect.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps us start the day calmly, teaches discipline, makes us thankful and gives peace of mind (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: They are named after the Sun, the Moon and five planets that people could see in the sky, so each day has a heavenly partner.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for Sun and Moon, planets and naming.

53. (5 marks)
   Answer: Morning prayer and Namaste (Prarthana, Paramatma), honest schoolwork (Dharma, Artha), helping a friend (Prani Daya), thinking about the day's good deeds (Punarjanam and karma).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each principle applied, up to 5.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hiranyakashipu was a proud king who wanted to be called God. His young son Prahlad kept praying to Vishnu. Lord Narsimha appeared from a pillar and defeated the king.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the proud king, 1 mark for Prahlad's faith, 1 mark for Narsimha.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: Bal Kaand and Ayodhya Kaand.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: Paramatma, Purushartha, Prani Daya, Punarjanam, Prarthana (any correct set earns marks).
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each, rounded up.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Ramayan: Hinduism. Kalpasutra: Jainism. Dhammapada: Buddhism. Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji: Sikhism.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each pair.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: It reminds us of Kenya's step to self-government on 1 June 1963, teaches patriotism and unity, and lets us respect the flag and the anthem.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.
